survey: A western covered cart on a dirt road, seen from the front-left. A wooden box body with a red top rail. A canvas cover on hoops sits over the back two-thirds of the box, and its arched front opening faces the driver. A plank driver's bench on two posts sits on the front (right) end of the box. One axle with two large spoked wheels sits a little behind the middle of the box. The near wheel stands outside the box side, and its top reaches the red rail. The far wheel shows under the box, offset to the right and higher up, which fits the perspective. A single tongue runs from the underside of the box's front corner down to the ground and ends in a crossbar resting on the dirt. With the tongue on the ground, the cart stands on three points: both wheels and the tongue. Wheels, box, cover and bench all attach plausibly, and the wheels and crossbar sit on the road.

errors.where: Tongue where it meets the front corner of the box
errors.what: The tongue just comes out of the bottom corner of the box. Nothing connects it to the axle or the frame under the box. It is also one central pole on a two-wheeled cart, where one horse would need a pair of shafts. As drawn, it could not take a pulling load.

fix: Attach the tongue to a visible wooden frame under the box that runs back to the wheel axle. Or replace the single pole with two parallel shafts, one on each side of the front of the cart, both resting on the ground.
